children: Eurozone industrial production fell again in July, highlighting the uneven nature of the region's economic recovery as manufacturers contend with higher energy costs despite signs of improving demand.

Industrial production fell 0.1% from the previous month, following a 0.1% fall in June, the statistics agency Eurostat said Wednesday. A consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a steeper fall of 0.4%.

The decline came despite signs that some manufacturers are becoming more optimistic about the outlook. According to purchasing managers' surveys by S&P Global, activity in the eurozone's manufacturing sector picked up in July and expanded at its fastest pace in more than four years in August.

The divergence between the survey data and official production figures partly reflects the weakness of some of Europe's biggest industrial economies. Industrial production in Germany, the eurozone's largest economy, fell 1.5% on month in July,  while output also retreated 0.4% in France, Eurostat data showed.
